2. Respondent No. 1 being plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Title Suit for declaration of title and also for a declaration that the treating of the suit property as vested and nonresident property is illegal and without jurisdiction. It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit property originally belonged to Kailash Chandra Das, Nitta Nanda Das and Radhakanta Das and their names were duly recorded in CS Khatian. By amicable partition the present suit property fell in the share of Nitta Nanda Das and this Nitta Nanda Das subsequently transferred the suit property to one Ram Chandra Paul by an amalnama in the year 1953 BS (1947 AD). The SA record was prepared in the name of Ram Chandra Paul. By an agreement dated 5.5.69 this Ram Chandra Paul sold his property to the present plaintiff and delivered possession of the suit property to the plaintiff on receipt of an earnest money amounting to Taka 50,000.00 out of total consideration money at Taka 80,000.00. After few months this Ram Chandra Paul died without executing and registering the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff. However, Gour Gopal Paul, the only son of Ram Chandra Paul, after receiving the balance consideration of Taka 30,000.00 executed and registered two sale deeds on 4.12.79 in favour of the plaintiff and thereby the plaintiff acquired right, title and possession in the suit property. The defendant had no right, title and interest in the suit property. It came to the knowledge of the plaintiff that the suit property was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 2 the Assistant Custodian, Vested and Non-Resident Property, in RS Khatian. This created some doubt about the title and possession of the plaintiff and that is why he filed the present suit for declaration that treating the suit property as vested and non resident property is illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 4. On the aforesaid pleadings of the parties four issues were framed by the trial Court which were considered and disposed of together. The plaintiff examined three witnesses including himself and the contesting defendant No. 2 examined one witness. The plaintiff submitted so many papers and documents which have been marked as exhibits. After considering the evidence on record the learned Subordinate Judge passed the judgment and decree in the aforesaid suit decreeing in favour of the plaintiff. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court dated 25.1.86 passed in Title Suit No. 553 of 1981 (formerly Title Suit No. 888 of 1979), the defendant No. 2 preferred this appeal. The plaintiff examined himself as PW 1. He reiterated his case as he stated in the plaint. He also proved the papers and documents, namely, Exts.-1 to 8(c). He categorically denied that his vendor Ram Chandra Paul did not leave this country in 1953. He stated that he purchased the suit property by two documents, Exts. 4 and 4(a) on payment of the balance consideration Taka 30,000.00. He further stated that it was wrongly recorded in RS Khatian in the name of defendant No. 2. Against this wrong recording, the plaintiff preferred appeal which was allowed and thereafter the name of the plaintiff was recorded instead of the defendant No. 2. 

 8. Ext-1 is the copy of CS parcha which was prepared in the name of three brothers who were the original owners of the suit property. Ext. 2 is the SA parcha prepared in the name of Ram Chandra Paul. Ext.-3 is the death certificate of Ram Chandra Paul which shows that Ram Chandra Paul died on 18.11.69 at 53, Piary Das Road, Dhaka. This certificate was obtained on 23.12.81 from the Dhaka Municipal Corporation. Exts. 4 and 4 (a) are the two registered documents executed and registered in favour of the plaintiff by Gour Chandra Paul, son of Ram Chandra Paul. Ext.-5 is the SA parcha prepared in the name of Ram Chandra Paul. Ext-6 is the copy of the Khatian prepared in the name of the present plaintiff. Ext. 7 is the certified copy of order-sheet of Case No. 605 of 1984 which was case for correction of record of rights in the name of the plaintiff and it appears that after considering the materials on record the name of the plaintiff was recorded in the record of rights after making necessary correction. Ext-8 is a rent receipt issued in the name of Ram Chandra Paul. Ext-8 (a) is another rent receipt in the name of Ram Chandra Paul, but rent was paid through the present plaintiff. Ext-8 (b) is a certificate of Mutation Officer which shows in the municipal corporation the name of the present plaintiff was mutated in respect of the suit property. Ext-8 (c) is another rent receipt in favour of the present plaintiff given by Dhaka Municipal Corporation. These are more or less the oral as well as documentary evidence of the parties.
